extracted.intended_audience: SBIR applicants and diagnostics product developers (entrepreneurs, engineers, and commercialization teams building point-of-care infectious disease tests)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for developing, validating, manufacturing, protecting IP for, and commercializing a point-of-care HIV 4th-generation (Ag/Ab) diagnostic device, oriented to an SBIR Phase II application and subsequent regulatory/market entry. Covers assay performance milestones, regulatory/QMS requirements, manufacturing and supply-chain scaling, IP strategy, and go-to-market/partnering approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO procurement criteria for limited resource environments
rubrics_metrics.description: For limited resource environments the diagnostics must operate on battery power, require no refrigeration and be simple to operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting WHO-defined criteria facilitates inclusion in bulk procurement schemes and adds credibility for UN procurement agencies, NGOs, Global Fund, Clinton Foundation, PEPFAR, AMDS, and other purchasers that rely on WHO guidance and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory quality system and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineering development of a medical device must occur under an established quality system that meets ISO 13485 and/or FDA QSR requirements, and must be documented in a Design History File (DHF) that is submitted to the FDA for regulatory approval. A Device Master Record (DMR) is also required that fully documents the bill of materials, approved suppliers, all hardware and software design specifications, and all manufacturing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality system implementation and a complete DHF/DMR are prerequisites for regulatory submissions; documentation must capture design, BOM, suppliers, software/hardware specs, and manufacturing processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management and human factors engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess and mitigate potential harm to the user and patient, risk management efforts incorporating human factors engineering must be fully documented throughout the product lifecycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human factors work should be integrated into design history and risk files and be part of pre-market evidence (usability data) used to support regulatory submissions and CLIA waiver claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay performance equivalence to FDA-approved 4th gen lab assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim milestone: an HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody detection assay with performance equivalent to FDA-approved laboratory 4th gen Ag/Ab combo assays for the MBio early/acute sample collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate analytic and clinical performance comparable to established lab analyzers (e.g., Abbott ARCHITECT) using panels and clinical specimens; this equivalence is a stated Aim milestone and central to validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation dataset size and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate system using well characterized early HIV infection specimens including a panel of 200 HIV positive specimens comprised of 20 acute infection samples (RNA+ / Ab -), early seroconversion (Western Blot indeterminate) and seropositive (HIV-1 and HIV-2) samples. 200 HIV-negative samples will be used for specificity testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sample numbers and the explicit inclusion of acute cases are the Aim 3 milestone for demonstrating clinical performance; follow panels and unique acute sample collections described in Aim 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-market field evaluation sample requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Place systems in intended use setting and capture operational and usability feedback; generate a preliminary dataset on capillary whole blood samples from 100 study participants in San Diego.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 4 milestone: field usability and operational data collected in intended settings to inform design lock and support pre-IDE discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic reactivity cutoff definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define cutoff as mean plus 5 standard deviations of no-target control samples (run in triplicate) for declaring reactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit statistical definition of cutoff used to claim analytic sensitivity; provides reproducible criterion for assessing assay signals vs controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device product requirements — multiplexed detection and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel HIV-1/2 antibody and p24 antigen detection on a single point-of-care platform; workflow and ease-of-use comparable to conventional HIV rapid tests; robust, low cost, minimally instrumented system for use in emergency departments, public health labs, STD clinics, and targeted outreach programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product must combine multiplexed detection with simple workflow and minimal instrumentation to meet intended-use settings and to compete with other POC solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat-stable reagent integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate heat stable assay reagents into the MQ cartridge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reagents must be formulated and validated for storage and transport in target climates and to meet procurement/field use expectations in resource-limited settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for manufacture / value engineering goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Material and labor costs must be substantially reduced from those of the prototype by transitioning from expensive machined components to injection-molded parts, re-designing electronics boards and optical components, tooling for efficient injection molding, and reducing labor time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific objectives include investment in mold tooling, investigating automation to reduce labor, validating laser welding of the cartridge, and validating multi-cavity mold tooling to move to high capacity production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply chain and contract manufacturer qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Ramping to projected volumes will require close partnerships with a variety of outside contract manufacturers (CM’s) that have been approved under MBio’s Supplier Quality Assurance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For instruments (1,000–10,000/yr) many CMs may suffice; for disposable cartridges (up to 20 million/yr) specialized high-capacity CM capability is required. Vet and qualify several CMs and choose based on quality system and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing capacity planning and staging
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial production, up to 2 million units per year, is being implemented in a new facility leased by MBio; as the product scales up, investigate CM’s for cartridge high-capacity production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan production staging: in-house or small-scale CM for instrument; new facility for initial cartridge volumes; identify large-scale CM partners for tens of millions of units.

rubrics_metrics.name: QA/QC responsibilities and location
rubrics_metrics.description: QA/QC done in-house for the instrument; the company must ensure manufacturing QA/QC capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of production partner, instrument QA/QC readiness in-house is expected; supplier quality assurance programs must be in place for outsourced components and cartridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property protection pillars
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three major pillars of our intellectual property strategy: (1) protect our ideas and methods via an exclusively licensed portfolio combined with new IP filings; (2) establish freedom to operate for our products through issued patents and supplemental analysis/licensing; (3) investigate blocking ability to extract royalties from infringing products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain exclusive license to foundational patents, file utility patents for new innovations, continue IP prosecution (dedicated staff and budget), and budget for freedom-to-operate analyses and opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and inventor assignment practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Require employees, consultants, outside collaborators and other advisors to execute confidentiality agreements upon commencement; agreements provide that inventions conceived during tenure are exclusive property of the company; documents are reviewed for confidential information prior to public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard employment/consulting contracts and disclosure controls are required as part of IP protection practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagent access — licensing and supply agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure licenses to and/or supply agreements for the reagents used in tests; anticipated to be achievable on commercially acceptable terms and a major driver for partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early identification and contracting for critical reagent supply is necessary for productization and partner negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom-to-operate diligence and budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to evaluate potential conflicts in relevant fields (waveguide sensors, fluorescence immunoassays, diagnostic microarrays) and budget for analysis and up to two freedom-to-operate opinions to clarify position for partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate specific budget and staff time for formal FTO analyses to support partner conversations and licensing negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue model alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue can come from (1) Sales of the instrument and test kits by MBio; (2) Royalties from the sales through strategic partners; (3) Licensing or sale of the Intellectual Property to a strategic partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider scenarios: retain rights and develop manufacturing/distribution; outsource sales/marketing to a distribution partner while retaining manufacturing oversight; or grant exclusive licenses. Hybrid approaches (e.g., geographic split licenses) are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go-to-market and distribution strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Roll out products through a combination of direct sales, strategic partnerships and independent distributors; marketing to raise awareness via trade shows, print advertising, special programs and distributor promotions; register diagnostics in a number of countries, progressing country by country in order of market size; enlist NGOs to raise awareness and facilitate acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target public health purchasers (countries, ministries of health, CDC, Global Fund), centralize purchasing channels where possible, and align registration/approval timelines with market roll-out plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage procurement and global health programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with partners and affiliates to be included in bulk procurement schemes and umbrella organizations (WHO, SCMS). Use AMDS and other WHO/UN mechanisms to ensure access to quality diagnostics at best prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion in procurement lists reduces price barriers and increases reach; designing product to meet these agencies' evaluation criteria is strategic for adoption in developing countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive-differentiation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate from lateral flow and competing POC technologies by offering higher sensitivity and specificity, lower sample volume, electronic readout and control features (procedure controls, operator lockout), higher throughput, simpler/more robust technology, and lower cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly benchmark against competitors (Alere, Trinity, OraSure, PIMA, Zyomyx, Daktari, HemoCue, Quest/LabCorp) and articulate measurable advantages (sensitivity, sample volume, readout, throughput, robustness, cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product robustness and throughput expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For the CD4 application the MBio system has significant throughput and cost advantages relative to Alere PIMA; aim for high throughput, simple technology (more robust), and lower per-test cost for POC use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design targets should include robustness in field conditions, per-test cost reduction, and throughput sufficient for intended clinical/public health workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of competitor market development
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a 'fast follower' market entry model: benefit from market development by competitors who are establishing the operational characteristics of POC CD4 testing; market introduction will benefit from acceptance fostered by early competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and messaging should leverage early adopters' efforts and published operational studies to accelerate uptake.
